chunks.text: Today, we will talk about Norway.
Norway is a cold, beautiful, and peaceful country in Northern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Norway?
Norway is in Northern Europe in a region called Scandinavia.
It is next to Sweden, Finland, and Russia.
To the west, it touches the Atlantic Ocean and the Norwegian Sea.
Norway has many mountains, forests, and fjords.
Fjords are deep water valleys.
What is the capital city of Norway?
The capital city is Oslo.
Oslo is a modern and green city.
It has museums, parks, shops, and a harbor.
Other cities include Bergen, famous for rain and fjords.
Trondheim, an old city with a big church.
Tromso in the north, good for seeing the northern lights.
How many people live in Norway?
About five, five million people live in Norway.
Most people live in the south, near the coast.
There are also many small towns and villages in the mountains and forests.
What language do people speak in Norway?
The official language is Norwegian.
There are two written forms, Buckmole and Nyorsk.
Many people also speak English very well.
Some people in the north speak Sami, the language of the indigenous Sami people.
What is the weather like in Norway?
Norway has four seasons, winter, cold and snowy, good for skiing.
Spring, fresh and green.
Summer, short but warm with long daylight.
Autumn, cool with red and yellow leaves.
In the north, the sun does not set in summer and does not rise in winter.
This is called the Midnight Sun and Polar Night.
What does Norway look like?
Norway has mountains and lakes, forests and rivers, fjords, deep sea valleys between cliffs, northern lights, dancing lights in the sky in winter.
It is a perfect place for nature lovers and outdoor sports.
What animals live in Norway?
In Norway, you can find moose, reindeer and foxes.
Wolves, lynx and bears in remote areas, eagles, owls and seabirds.
Whales, seals and fish in the sea.
In the far north, people use reindeer for transport and food.
What do people eat in Norway?
Norwegian food is often simple, fresh and made with local ingredients.
People eat fish like salmon and cod, potatoes, cabbage and bread, meat like lamb pork and sometimes reindeer, berries like blueberries and cloudberries.
Popular dishes, forry kohl, lamb stew with cabbage, rackfisk, fermented fish for special occasions.
Chutkaker, meatballs with gravy, lefse sweet flatbread, waffles with jam and sour cream.
What do people drink in Norway?
People drink water.
Norway has very clean tap water.
Coffee, Norwegians drink a lot of coffee, milk and fruit juice.
Adults may drink beer, cider or a strong drink called akavit.
Hot drinks are popular in the cold weather.
What is life like in Norway?
Life in Norway is quiet, safe and comfortable.
People enjoy spending time in nature, skiing, hiking, fishing, being with family, reading books, listening to music and visiting cafes, working during the week and relaxing on weekends.
People love a lifestyle called free -lifts live.
It means open air living.
What are some holidays and traditions in Norway?
National Day, May 17th with parades and flags.
Christmas with lights, songs and traditional food.
Easter, often celebrated in mountain cabins.
Midsummer, St.
Hans with bonfires in June.
Sami National Day, February 6th.
People wear traditional clothes called bunat on special days.
Some fun facts about Norway.
Norway is one of the richest and most peaceful countries in the world.
It has over 1,000 fjords.
Vikings lived in Norway over 1,000 years ago.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo.
Norwegians love skiing.
It's called their national sport.
Now you know many things about Norway.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the nature, traditions and lifestyle.
Great job.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
